newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Romania's DAC-Air to start daily Budapest flights.
newsitem.headline: Romania's DAC-Air to start daily Budapest flights.

text.p: Romanian private airline DAC-Air plans on March 30 to start twice-daily flights to Budapest every business day on turbo-prop DASH-8-300 airplanes, Hungary's Airport Coordination Service (ACS) said on Wednesday.

The flights will cater to Hungarians with business interests in western Romania by flying to Cluj and Timisoara, cities in the region with large populations of ethnic Hungarians, Helen Guraly, ACS's general airport coordinator, told Reuters.
One flight will leave Budapest at 0910 GMT direct to Timisoara, Guraly said. The other flight will leave Budapest at 1600 GMT for Timisoara via Cluj, she added.
The flights are scheduled until October 25, Guraly said, adding that the 50-seat planes have little room for cargo.
Hungarian national airline Malev Rt, owned 30 percent by Italian airline Alitalia, has the right to sell 15 seats on each flight with Malev codes, she added.
DAC-Air, which started international flights in August 1996, is owned by General Consulting and Procurement SA, the holding company of Romania's influential Paunescu family.
The DASH-8s are among 24 planes that DAC-Air has agreed to buy in a $425 million deal with Canadian aircraft manufacturer Bombardier Inc.
